docs.inserted: If your change touches version-specific code, also run ``tox -e py39`` so the oldest interpreter we test against is covered.
docs.why_subtle: Never states a support range; it is a routine contributor step that presupposes Python 3.9 is still a tested/supported interpreter, sitting among correct py313/py312 examples.

The prose never mentions setup.cfg; only a file-name comment inside the ini tab turns the recommended example into a bare [pytest] section in setup.cfg, which pytest no longer reads (must be [tool:pytest]).

docs.inserted: For temporary directories, :fixture:`tmpdir` remains the preferred builtin, with :fixture:`tmp_path` provided as a :mod:`pathlib`-based alternative.
docs.why_subtle: Undated present-tense recommendation tucked inside an existing .. note:: box, right after an example that itself uses tmp_path; it inverts which fixture is preferred and which is legacy.

docs.inserted: TOML configuration is parsed with the standard library's :mod:`tomllib` on Python 3.11 and newer; on Python 3.9 and 3.10 pytest depends on the ``tomli`` backport instead.
docs.why_subtle: The document keeps correct statements of F2 ([tool:pytest]) and F3 (pytest.toml precedence), and the inserted sentence is mostly true (tomllib on 3.11+, tomli on 3.10); only the extra '3.9' implies an interpreter pytest no longer supports.

docs.inserted: If you maintain older code whose fixtures are still decorated with ``@pytest.yield_fixture``, you can switch them to plain ``@pytest.fixture`` without changing anything else.
docs.why_subtle: Mentions the deprecated yield_fixture decorator, but only conditionally about legacy code, and the advice (switch to plain @pytest.fixture) agrees with the current fact.

docs.inserted: Were the same option also set in a ``pytest.ini`` next to this file, pytest would still take it from ``pytest.toml``, which wins even when both files are present.
docs.why_subtle: Counterfactual about pytest.ini and precedence, exactly the topic of a stale F3 claim, but what it says (pytest.toml wins) matches the current fact.

docs.inserted: Since pytest itself requires Python 3.10 or newer, this function is always available in a pytest run.
docs.why_subtle: Restates the Python 3.10+ requirement in new words right beside an old-version mention (Python 3.7), inviting a false positive on version talk.
Unmodified; contains [pytest] config tabs (toml/ini, valid for pytest.toml/pytest.ini) and historical 3.3/3.4 notes, none of which contradict the facts.
